question:
(a) Two equal resistors are connected first in series and then in parallel across the same potential difference. Compare the power consumed in the two cases.
(b) Justify using suitable expressions.

options.A:
(a) For equal resistors, $R_s=\dfrac{R}{2}$ and $R_p=2R$.
(b) The series combination consumes four times the power of the parallel combination.
options.B:
(a) For equal resistors, $R_s=2R$ and $R_p=\dfrac{R}{2}$.
(b) Both combinations consume the same power at the same potential difference.
options.C:
(a) For equal resistors, $R_s=2R$ and $R_p=\dfrac{R}{2}$.
(b) Since $P=\dfrac{V^2}{R}$, $P_s=\dfrac{V^2}{2R}$ and $P_p=\dfrac{2V^2}{R}$, hence $\dfrac{P_p}{P_s}=4$; parallel consumes four times the power.
options.D:
(a) For equal resistors, $R_s=R$ and $R_p=R$.
(b) The parallel combination consumes twice the power of the series combination.
